checks.what: Ottoman gain of Bosnia and Herzegovina from nobody, January 1890. The page says the Treaty of Berlin 'caused Bosnia and Herzegovina to nominally remain under sovereignty of the Ottoman Empire' until the 1908 annexation, recognised 26 February 1909. The country spec is 191 cells. In the trial, 180 become Ottoman land occupied by Austria-Hungary at 1 January 1900; the other 11 were already Austro-Hungarian or Serb. The Ottoman 1895 snap leaves them, because occupied cells are left to their relation. It bridges a gap whose root is in 1878 (see problems).

Austro-Hungarian occupation of Ottoman Bosnia, restarted in February 1890. The page supports it: 'The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878', and annexation came in 1908. The trial merges it into the relation of austria-hungary/ledger/1, which now covers 184 cells (Bosnia plus the Sanjak). But the note quoted 'Austria occupied (but did not annex)', which is not on the cited page.
checks.fix: Replaced the note's quote with the page's own words: 'The occupation ... started on 29 July 1878', the Treaty of Berlin's 'shall be occupied and administered by Austria-Hungary', and 'In 1908 ... formally annexing the occupied zone'.

checks.what: Ethiopian gain of Gimirra, 1898. The page says: 'Finally, also in 1898, Ras Tassama annexed Massonge and Gimirra.' The Gimirra region is 73 cells (bbox 34.9-36.2 E, 6.2-7.5 N, the Bench country), nobody's before and Ethiopian after. Massonge is rightly dropped: there is no gazetteer name for it.

Omani gain of Dhofar from nobody, 1890, a bridge event at confidence 2. The page says Fadl bin Alawi 'was expelled by local sheikhs in January 1879' and that Sayyid Turki 'established his rule there'. The page gives no date for that rule. This matches sultanate-of-oman/ledger/15 (1879) and the dossier's 1898 keyframe ('the sultan's own province'). The Zufar spec is 648 cells; at 1900, 627 are Omani and 21 are Aden's. The Oman 1898 snap now adds 2 cells instead of 446. Dhofar stays grey in 1880-1889 (see problems).

USA 1890 keyframe: the Cliopatria shape plus the modern country (less Alaska and Hawaii), plus the Alaska region. This is the same form as the dossier's own 1868-1880 corrections. The page backs the Great Lakes waters inside the states: 'in addition to 38,575 square miles (99,910 km2) of Great Lakes waters' and 'Michigan's western boundaries are almost entirely water boundaries'. The 1890 snap now removes 0 cells instead of 779. New conflicts are only logged: british-colonial-empire keeps 29 cells a year (R1) and Mexico keeps 15 border cells (size rule). No land changes hands. Hawaii is correctly left out.

French Africa 1897 keyframe: Cliopatria 1895 plus Madagascar, the Mossi kingdoms and Gwiriko. Bobo-Dioulasso page: 'On September 25, 1897, the French briefly occupied Sia', then 'On November 23rd a military post was established' and became the headquarters of the cercle. History of Burkina Faso page: 'The French arrived and claimed the area in 1896'. The Mossi spec resolves to the same 301 cells as mossi-kingdoms/ledger/3, and the Gwiriko spec is identical to gwiriko/ledger/2 (126 cells). Snaps run after the year's events, so Gwiriko turns French only after its September 1897 dissolve. The 1897 snap now removes 37 cells instead of 464. Caveat: the why quotes only half of the History of Burkina Faso sentence (see problems).

French Africa 1898 keyframe: Cliopatria 1898 plus Madagascar, Mossi, Gwiriko and Chari-Baguirmi (181 cells). The page supports Bagirmi: Gaourang appealed to the French, 'making Bagirmi a French protectorate after the signing of a treaty in 1897'. But the whole Chari-Baguirmi province took 17 of Rabih's Kotoko cells round N'Djamena by R2 in 1898. Rabih held them until 1900: the page says 'In 1900 the combined forces of the French and Bagirmi killed az-Zubayr', and state-of-rabih-az-zubayr/ledger/9 dates the loss to April 1900.
checks.fix: Cut Rabih's own region ({place: N'Djamena, km 60, country Chad}) from the Chari-Baguirmi element. In the re-run trial Rabih keeps all 43 cells of that disc at 1 January 1900. The 1898 snap removes 18 cells and adds 11; the uncut file added 28.

checks.what: Ethiopia 1895 keyframe: the Cliopatria shape without Afar, plus the conquests of 1886-1894. The page supports every date: Arsi 1886, Wollega 1886, Harar after Chelenqo on 6 January 1887, Illubabor 1887, Gurage 1889, Hadiya 1879-1884, Kambata 'occupied since 1890' and completed 1893, 'Bale, Sidamo (excluding Borana), the Ogaden, and Welayta were occupied from 1891 onward', Gofa and Wollamo 1894. The Ogaden spec is the whole Somali region of Ethiopia (1363 cells), as in the dossier's ledger/39. The 1895 snap now removes 0 cells instead of 867. But the Illubabor and Wollega polygons reach into the Kingdom of Jimma's 80 km core, and R2 gave it to Ethiopia: the uncut patch left Jimma 2 of its 84 core cells. The page says 'Jimma, Limmu, Gera, and Guma became tributary regions' (1881), so Jimma was not annexed.
checks.fix: Wrapped the correction as minus [the same union, {place: Jima, km 80}], which is the kingdom-of-jimma dossier's own keyframe region. The same cut was made in keyframe_overrides/4 and /6. In the re-run trial Jimma keeps all 84 core cells, and the Ethiopia/Jimma R2 conflict drops from 114 to 59 cell-years (published compile: 114).

checks.what: Ethiopia 1898 keyframe: as the 1895 one, plus three pieces. Borana: 'In 1896-1897, expeditions were launched into Borana'; it is 199 cells, of which 17 lie in Kenya and are kept by british-africa (R1). Beni Shangul: 'In 1898, Beni Shangul and the border with Sudan were controlled'; this takes 9 cells from anglo-egyptian-sudan. Gimirra (1898). The 1898 snap now removes 12 cells instead of 278. It had the same Jimma overlap as keyframe_overrides/3.
checks.fix: The same {place: Jima, km 80} cut as keyframe_overrides/3.

checks.what: USA 1898 keyframe: the dossier's 1898 correction (without Cuba; with Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines) plus the modern country and Alaska, which carry the Great Lakes waters. Same reason and page as keyframe_overrides/0. The snap runs after the 1898 events, so Hawaii (annexed August) and the December cessions are already American when it applies. Nothing in it reaches beyond the dossier's own verdict except the lake and Alaska cells.

Ethiopia 1890 keyframe: the Cliopatria shape without Afar, plus Wollega, Arsi, Harar, Illubabor, Gurage and Hadiya. The page dates all of them before 1890 (Arsi 'completely in 1886', 'Ras Gobana Dacche occupy Wollega in 1886', Harar 'annexed to the Kingdom of Shewa' after Chelenqo in January 1887, Illubabor the following year, 'in 1889, the entire Gurage region was annexed', Hadiya 1879-1884). The 1890 snap now removes 0 cells instead of 402. It had the same Jimma overlap as keyframe_overrides/3: the Illubabor addition took Jimma core cells by R2.
checks.fix: The same {place: Jima, km 80} cut as keyframe_overrides/3.

checks.what: Ruling for Ethiopia over the Khedivate of Egypt, 1890-1899, inside modern Ethiopia. The Khedivate page has 'Egyptians withdrew in April 1884' and the 1884 Hewett Treaty. It settles 122 cell-years; at 1900, 78 cells pass from Egypt to Ethiopia, 71 of them in the Somali region. The why quoted 'Harar was annexed to the Kingdom of Shewa' as if it came from the cited page. That sentence is on the Menelik II page.
checks.fix: Attributed the quote in the why to the Menelik II page, after Chelenqo on 6 January 1887.

patch_check: --check-patch p1890-p1899 after the reviewer's fixes: 12 entries, 12 ok, 0 rejected. Re-run trial of the corrected file: all 12 applied; the ruling settles 122 cell-years. At the p1900 end anchor 2906 cells change owner against the published compile: nobody to Ethiopia 1139, nobody to the USA 779, nobody to French Africa 627, nobody to the Ottoman Empire (Bosnia, occupied by Austria-Hungary) 180, Egypt to Ethiopia 78, Ethiopia back to Jimma 72, Jimma to Ethiopia 17 (in the 80-110 km ring, Jimma's undated Badi-Folla stand-in), Anglo-Egyptian Sudan to Ethiopia 9 (Beni Shangul). The top-level note was also corrected: it listed 'Cuba occupation roles' events that the patch does not contain.
problems: Bosnia root cause, dossier request. ottoman-empire/ledger/192 (July 1878) records a 'loss' of Bosnia to austria-hungary, while austria-hungary/ledger/2 occupies Ottoman Bosnia. Together with the austria-hungary_1880 keyframe this leaves Bosnia nobody's in 1880-1889. It also leaves a reversed occupation relation (austria-hungary/ledger/2: occupier ottoman-empire, owner austria-hungary) on 10 cells along the 1873 border, from 1878 to at least 1900. Fix the Ottoman ledger, not the window patches. The p1900-p1909 trial should check that austria-hungary/ledger/4 (October 1908) closes the Bosnia part of the merged relation, now that events/1 has joined it to the Sanjak relation of ledger/1.
Dhofar is still grey in 1880-1889. The root fix is a sultanate-of-oman_1880 keyframe override adding {admin1: Zufar, country: Oman}, for window p1880-p1889; events/3 only bridges from 1890.

Keyframes in the next window will undo this window's gains. The 1900 keyframes are unadjusted Cliopatria shapes, so in p1900-p1909, french-africa_1900 drops Mossi, Gwiriko and Bagirmi, ethiopian-empire_1900 drops the Ogaden and the other conquests, and the USA keyframes from 1900 drop the Great Lakes waters. The ethiopian-empire Cliopatria keyframes from 1900 to 1932 will also take Jimma's core by R2 again unless they cut {place: Jima, km 80}.

Jimma is drawn as an independent kingdom. ethiopian-empire/ledger/30 starts its vassal relation with the name 'Gibe Oromo states (Jimma, Limmu, Gera, Guma)', not the slug kingdom-of-jimma, so the tributary status the Menelik II page gives ('Jimma, Limmu, Gera, and Guma became tributary regions', 1881) draws no vassal tint. Dossier request, or a patch event vassal_start ethiopian-empire -> kingdom-of-jimma, 1881.

The Kaffa country south of Jimma is nobody's in 1899. kingdom-of-kaffa holds no cells, and ethiopian-empire/ledger/49-50 take Kaffa only in 1900, while the Menelik II page says it was 'completely conquered' in 1896-1900. Left; it needs a page with a date.

Mossi: the History of Burkina Faso page says 'The French arrived and claimed the area in 1896, but Mossi resistance ended only with the capture of their capital Ouagadougou in 1901'. keyframe_overrides/1 quotes only the first half. The dossier draws the plateau as plain French land from 1896 (mossi-kingdoms dissolves 1896), so a French contest until 1901 may be wanted. Dossier decision.
One khedivate-of-egypt cell remains in Somaliland at the end of 1899, outside rulings/0's region. Minor.

The window agent's Cuba issue (US land drawn as occupied by a Republic of Cuba that did not exist until 1902) and the USA Great Lakes gap in keyframes up to p2000 remain dossier requests. No Cuba entry is in the patch.
